acceptance_checks.finding: The preserved low, straight-sided, neckless jar, very wide open mouth and active spoon make refrigerated spoonable yogurt legible before luxury packaging.

The edit preserves the majority transparent food-bearing area, neutral ivory yogurt, restrained amber honey fold and actual-scale thyme flecks. The 60–70% visibility result remains a visual estimate pending physical dieline measurement.

The partial fibrous label now retains only MORA, THYME HONEY, GREEK YOGURT, 150 g and the seven requested food-process fields with simple open leader lines and one small check mark. Enclosing cells and dense pharmacy-like ruling are gone.

Original-detail inspection confirms that the right regulatory column, circular GR/date emblem, fabricated dates and numbers, recycling icon, KJ initials, names, lot values, seals and certification-like marks are absent.
The stainless spoon, rim overlap, yogurt contact and firm broken-edge furrow remain physically plausible after the label-only edit.

The upper-left 30–35% remains quiet, object-free graphite and can carry a headline. The preserved diagonal stainless work-surface edge still enters the lower-left zone, so CTA placement and responsive crops require layout testing.
The uncoated-looking label remains limited to the front-right portion and does not become a collar, sleeve or full wrap.
Glass wall thickness, rim highlights, base weight, paper fibers, spoon reflection and grounded contact shadow remain coherent; no unrelated scene redesign is visible.
The jar and food remain neutrally lit and readable while the graphite manufactory recedes into preserved shadow detail.

No fabricated legal or traceability data remain in the hero. Final commercial packaging still requires a separate market-approved legal-information solution and real production records outside this conceptual image.

issues.issue: The lower-left copy-safe field contains the preserved edge and tonal transition of the stainless work surface.
issues.action: Keep headline in the upper-left zone and test CTA placement at desktop and responsive crops.
